alerts.title: Coastal Flood Watch issued November 24 at 4:57PM EST until November 27 at 1:00PM EST by NWS Upton NY
alerts.area: Hudson; Eastern Bergen; Eastern Essex; Eastern Union
alerts.description: * WHAT...1 1/2 to 2 feet of inundation above ground level possible in vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline. * WHERE...Hudson, Eastern Bergen, Eastern Essex and Eastern Union Counties. * WHEN...From Thursday morning through Friday afternoon high tides. * COASTAL FLOOD IMPACTS...Widespread minor to moderate flooding of vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline, including roads, parking lots, parks, lawns, and homes and businesses with basements near the waterfront. Numerous road closures are likely, and vehicles parked in vulnerable areas near the waterfront will likely become flooded. Flooding will also extend inland from the waterfront along tidal rivers and bays, including the tidal portions of the Hackensack River and Passaic Rivers. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The highest water levels are likely with the Thursday morning and evening high tides, potentially extending into the Friday morning high tides. The forecast has been leaned towards a higher end water level scenario to provide a bit of safety margin. If the timing of strongest winds is quicker than currently forecast the peak water level forecast could be increased by a few tenths for Thursday morning. if slower the Thursday morning forecast could be lowered slightly.
alerts.instruction: If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property.

Many roads become impassable. Some damage to vulnerable structures may begin to occur. At this level, flooding may become severe enough to cause structural damage along with widespread roadway flooding in coastal and bayside communities, and near inland tidal waterways. Some locations may become isolated by the flood waters. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Minor tidal flooding is expected on Wednesday morning. The most severe and impactful high tide will be with Thursday morning's high tide, where major tidal flooding is possible.
alerts.instruction: A Coastal Flood Warning means that moderate or major tidal flooding is occurring or imminent. Be prepared for rising water levels and take appropriate action to protect life and property. Follow the recommendations of local emergency management officials. Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The water may be deeper than you think it is. You will be putting yourself in danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to costly repairs. Visit the National Water Prediction Service at https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and flood impact information for your local tide gauge.
